=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/stage_workflow_support.sh: stage_self_repo_validation_renderer_entry, lines 826-829 (destination safety check); the sibling stage_self_repo_validation_template_entry at lines 781-789 walks every parent component | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The new function mirrors the existing trusted-template staging helper but its destination-safety check only inspects the leaf path (scripts/render_validation_templates.py) for a symlink. The trusted-template sibling (lines 781-789) walks every parent component of repo_path and refuses when any of them is a symlink, and that contract is precisely the one the new helper is supposed to satisfy — the PR description explicitly says the renderer "refuses a symlinked or non-file destination" like a missing template, and the trusted-template path is the only "exactly like a missing template" precedent in the same script. A checked-out integration branch (orchestrator/project-…) that makes scripts a symlink pointing outside the workspace is therefore not caught: mkdir -p on the parent of a symlink follows the link, and cp --remove-destination -- copies the trusted renderer through it, writing the verified renderer file somewhere outside the validation workspace before validation runs.
  WHY: a self-repo validate run on an integration branch whose scripts/ is a symlink would record VALIDATE_TRUSTED_RENDERER as if the renderer were staged into the validated workspace, while the trusted renderer is actually written to the symlink target. The next phase would then either pick up the symlinked file as a real staged copy (passing record_fetched_script and the log line without warning) or, if the symlink target is read-only, fail in a way that points at the wrong path. The sibling helper's parent-walk loop exists exactly to make this fail closed with ::error::Refusing symlinked validation-harness template path, and the PR's stated intent is that the renderer uses the same hardening.
- scripts/stage_workflow_support.sh: stage_self_repo_validation_renderer_entry, lines 833-837 (cp and chmod sequence, no && / set -e / explicit return check) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: cp --remove-destination -- is followed unconditionally by chmod +x and record_fetched_script. If cp fails (EIO, ENOSPC, permission denied, source-missing race), chmod +x still runs on whatever file already exists at repo_path from a previous run, then record_fetched_script records it as staged and a VALIDATE_TRUSTED_RENDERER success line is printed, even though no trusted bytes were actually written. The existing trusted-template entry (lines 797-799) silently has the same shape, so the new helper is at least consistent, but the file the trusted renderer is meant to guarantee is not the one that ends up on disk. Because the new function is the only path that puts a verified renderer into the validation checkout on an out-of-sync integration branch (the very scenario run 37925800341 hit), a silent failure here reproduces the original bug with a different error string downstream.
  WHY: a partial write or copy error during validation bootstrap would leave the stale renderer in place, log a green VALIDATE_TRUSTED_RENDERER line, and surface the harness_error from validation with no signal that staging actually failed. A simple `cp ... && chmod ... || exit 1` (or checking $? after cp) would surface the failure before the success log.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
